facts.statement: Simurghia was described in 2018 by Nicholas R. Longrich, David M. Martill, and Brian Andres.
facts.quote: It was published in 2018 by paleontologists Nicholas R. Longrich, David M. Martill, and Brian Andres

facts.statement: All known Simurghia fossils were found during a three-year excavation that recovered approximately 200 pterosaur specimens.
facts.quote: All known specimens of Simurghia were uncovered in a 3-year dig that unearthed about 200 pterosaur specimens.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Simurghia is a nearly complete humerus missing the head and ulnar crest.
facts.quote: The type specimen, FSAC-OB 7, consists of a nearly complete humerus, lacking only the humeral head and the ulnar crest.

facts.statement: The genus name Simurghia honors a flying beast from Persian mythology.
facts.quote: Simurghia is named after a flying beast from Persian mythology known as the Simurgh.

facts.statement: The species name robusta is Latin for "robust."
facts.quote: The species name, S. robusta, is a Latin word that means "robust."

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus lamegoi was transferred to the genus Simurghia in 2024.
facts.quote: In 2024, "Nyctosaurus" lamegoi was assigned as a species of Simurghia.

facts.statement: Simurghia lived in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Simurghia is a genus of pterosaur from the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco, a basin that dates to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, about 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Simurghia fossils were found in upper Maastrichtian phosphates in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Northern Morocco.
facts.quote: Simurghia was discovered in upper Maastrichtian phosphates located in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Northern Morocco.

facts.statement: The layer containing Simurghia dates to about one million years before the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: This layer dates back to the latest Maastrichtian, about 1 million years before the extinction event at the end of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The time range for Simurghia is estimated from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Simurghia as the sister taxon to Alcione elainus within the family Nyctosauridae.
facts.quote: In this analysis, they found Simurghia to be the sister taxon of the species Alcione elainus, both placed within the family Nyctosauridae.

facts.statement: Simurghia belongs to the clade Aponyctosauria.
facts.quote: These taxa, along with the Nyctosauridae, comprise the clade Aponyctosauria.

facts.statement: Longrich and colleagues determined that Simurghia is a member of the family Nyctosauridae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético realizado por Longrich et al. determinó que Simurghia es un miembro de Nyctosauridae.

facts.statement: Simurghia is estimated to have had a wingspan of 5 meters.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have a wingspan of 5 m.

facts.statement: Isometric scaling suggests Simurghia weighed 560% more than Alcione, indicating they were distinct species rather than sexual dimorphs or age variants.
facts.quote: Using isometric scaling, Simurghia would weigh 560% more than Alcione, making sexual dimorphism or intraspecific variation unlikely.

facts.statement: Simurghia is similar in form but larger than Alcione and unlikely to represent an adult of that species.
facts.quote: Simurghia tiene una forma similar aunque mayor a la de Alcione, pero es improbable que represente un adulto de esa especie.

facts.statement: The region where Simurghia lived contained a diverse marine ecosystem including sharks, bony fish, turtles, plesiosaurs, and mosasaurs.
facts.quote: A large variety of marine life is known from the region, including sharks and bony fish, in addition to turtles, plesiosaurs and mosasaurs.
